title: How Non-Nigerian Africans Can Invest in the Dangote IPO
summary: Not every African country has access to the Dangote Refinery IPO yet. See which countries qualify and follow the step-by-step guide to invest on Bamboo.
body_markdown:
**In short:** You don’t need to be Nigerian to invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO on Bamboo, but eligibility depends on where you live. Through a Nominee Beneficiary account, more than 50 African countries are supported, and you’ll need a residential address in one of them plus a passport from any supported African country. Only Ghana, Kenya, Eswatini, and South Africa are currently excluded. This guide covers who qualifies and the full steps to apply. This is general information, not advice.


If you’re African and not Nigerian, the good news is that eligibility for the Dangote Refinery IPO is broader than most people assume. Bamboo’s Nominee Beneficiary account covers more than 50 African countries, which is most of the continent. There are just four notable exceptions, and if you happen to live in one of them, it’s better to know that upfront than to get partway through onboarding first.


This guide sets out exactly how eligibility works, the full list of supported countries, and once you’ve confirmed you qualify, the steps to apply. It is general information, not investment advice.


## How eligibility actually works


Two things determine whether you can apply, and they don’t have to be the same country.


**Where you live.** You need a residential address in a country Bamboo currently supports for this route. This is the harder gate of the two, and it’s the one worth checking first.


**The passport you hold.** You need an international passport from any supported African country, not necessarily the one you live in. So a Cameroonian living in Angola, for example, can apply using an Angolan residential address together with either a Cameroonian passport or a passport from Angola or another supported country. Where you live is what mainly determines eligibility; the passport just needs to be from somewhere on the supported list.


## The full list of supported countries


More than 50 African countries are currently supported as residence countries for the Nominee Beneficiary account, grouped here by region:


**North Africa:** Algeria, Egypt, Libya, Morocco, Sudan, Tunisia


**West Africa:** Benin, Burkina Faso, Cabo Verde, Côte d’Ivoire, The Gambia, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, Togo


**Central Africa:** Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Republic of the Congo, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Equatorial Guinea, Gabon, São Tomé and Príncipe


**East Africa:** Burundi, Comoros, Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia, Madagascar, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Rwanda, Seychelles, Somalia, South Sudan, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia, Zimbabwe


**Southern Africa:** Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Namibia


If your country is on this list, you can apply using a residential address there, together with a passport from any supported African country on the same list, not necessarily the same one you reside in.


## Countries not currently supported


**Ghana, Kenya, Eswatini, and South Africa are not currently supported** as residence countries for this route. If you live in one of these four countries, you cannot apply from there today, even though Bamboo operates directly in some of these markets for other products.


This isn’t necessarily permanent. Broader access to the NGX for residents of Ghana and South Africa through this same Nominee route is planned for the future, though it isn’t live yet, and it isn’t specific to the Dangote Refinery IPO. This article will be updated once that changes.


## Confirming your own country


The list above reflects the current supported countries, but eligibility can change over time, so if you want to double-check before you start, open the[Bamboo app](https://investbamboo.app.link/dangote-ipo-articles?%243p=a_custom_1626873672854248151) , begin the Dangote IPO application or sign-up flow, and look for the citizenship or country selector. If your country appears there, you’re eligible to proceed.


## If you live outside Africa entirely


Bamboo lets people sign up for the Dangote IPO from a wide range of countries across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and the Americas, in addition to Africa. But signing up and completing verification are different things. If you’re an African living outside the continent altogether, you can currently browse and start the sign-up process, but you cannot complete identity verification through this route yet, because verification currently requires a residential address in one of the African countries listed above, wherever your passport is from.


## What you need to apply


Once you’ve confirmed your country of residence is supported, here’s what to have ready: an international passport from any supported African country, your residential address details, a phone number you can receive a verification code on, and a way to fund a USD wallet, either a Misan virtual account or a USD debit or credit card, with at least $100 to deposit.


## Step by step: how to invest


1. **[Download the Bamboo app](https://investbamboo.app.link/dangote-ipo-articles?%243p=a_custom_1626873672854248151)** from the App Store or Google Play.
2. **Look for “Invest in Dangote IPO”** on the app’s landing screen, or start creating an account and the same option will appear.
3. **Choose your citizenship.** This determines which passport you’ll use to verify your identity, and it doesn’t have to be the country you currently live in.
4. **Enter your residential address** , including your country, state or region, and full address, in the supported African country where you actually live.
5. **Verify your identity.** Scan your passport, then take a selfie when prompted. Good lighting and a steady, unblurred shot speed this up.
6. **Create a 4-digit PIN** to secure your account.
7. **Add your next-of-kin details** : their name, how they’re related to you, and a phone number for them.
8. **Fill in your investment profile.** A short set of questions on your employment, marital status, investing goal, timeline, experience, and risk tolerance. This is standard onboarding, not something unique to you.
9. **Let verification complete.** Your account may briefly show as under review. This is a genuine check, so give it a little time rather than assuming something’s wrong.
10. **Fund your USD wallet** with at least $100, using Misan or a USD card.
11. **Subscribe.** Find the “Dangote IPO now live” banner on your home screen or in the Assets tab, choose your number of shares (minimum 10, at ₦525 each), pick your payment method, and confirm.


## Funding your wallet from abroad


[Misan](https://misan.app.link/NMBL1jwwg6b?%243p=a_custom_1625838821776661357) , Bamboo’s remittance app, lets you fund your wallet by bank transfer through a personal virtual account, in USD, GBP, EUR, or CAD. Deposit fees are small and vary by currency, roughly 0.1% on GBP and EUR, 0.5% on USD, each with a modest minimum and maximum charge. Your virtual account is typically ready within about an hour.


A USD debit or credit card, processed through Paystack or Flutterwave, is quicker if you already have one, though it carries a processing fee of around 2.9%.


Subscribing to the Dangote Refinery IPO itself is free either way, zero commission. The fees above belong to whichever funding method you pick, not to the investment.


## What happens after you apply


There’s nothing more to do once you’ve subscribed. After the offer closes, the SEC clears the Basis of Allotment, your shares are credited to your account, and if you were allotted fewer shares than you applied for, or none, the shortfall is returned automatically to your Bamboo wallet. Our guide on[everything you need to know about the Dangote Refinery IPO](https://learn.investbamboo.com/dangote-refinery-ipo-everything-you-need-to-know/) covers the full timetable. Withdrawing from your USD wallet later carries a $45 fee and typically takes five to seven business days.


## A word on getting this right


Only invest money you can afford to have tied up and, ultimately, to lose. Never borrow to fund an application, and always apply through the official Bamboo app rather than any third party claiming to help you “get in” from abroad. Our[Don’ts of Investing](https://learn.investbamboo.com/the-donts-of-investing-10-things-nigerian-investors-should-never-do/) series covers these principles in more depth.


## Frequently asked questions


**Can Cameroonians invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** Yes, Cameroon is a supported country, whether you live in Cameroon or another supported African country.


**Can Angolans invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** Yes, Angola is a supported country.


**Can Egyptians or Moroccans invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** Yes, both Egypt and Morocco are supported countries.


**Can Ethiopians, Kenyans, or Tanzanians invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** Ethiopia and Tanzania are supported. Kenya is the exception here and is not currently supported as a residence country.


**Can Ghanaians invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** Not currently, if you live in Ghana. Broader NGX access for Ghana through the same Nominee route is planned, but not yet live and not specific to this IPO.


**Can Kenyans invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** Not currently. Kenya is not supported as a residence country for this route at the moment.


**Can South Africans invest in the Dangote Refinery IPO?** Not currently, if you live in South Africa. Broader NGX access for South Africa is planned for the future, but not yet live.


**Is Eswatini supported?** No, not currently.


**My country isn’t in the four exceptions or the region lists above. Am I eligible?** If your country appears in the full list above, under any of the five regions, you’re eligible to apply. Only Ghana, Kenya, Eswatini, and South Africa are currently excluded across the whole of Africa.


**Do my passport and my country of residence have to be the same?** No. You need a passport from any supported African country and a residential address in a supported African country, but they don’t have to match.


**Does it cost anything to invest?** Subscribing to the Dangote Refinery IPO carries zero commission on Bamboo. Funding your wallet may carry a small fee depending on the method you choose.

## Ready to invest?


[Download the Bamboo app](https://investbamboo.app.link/dangote-ipo-articles?%243p=a_custom_1626873672854248151) , check the citizenship selector to confirm your country qualifies, and follow the steps above to apply. The Dangote Refinery IPO window closes on 13 October 2026.


### Quick Summary


This guide explains how non-Nigerian Africans can invest in the Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals IPO through Bamboo's Nominee Beneficiary account (also known as the NGX Nominee Account), and which African countries currently qualify. Eligibility depends on two things: a residential address in a supported African country, and an international passport from any supported African country; these do not have to be the same country. More than 50 African countries are supported, spanning North, West, Central, East, and Southern Africa; only Ghana, Kenya, Eswatini, and South Africa are currently excluded, though broader NGX access for Ghana and South Africa through the same Nominee route is planned for the future. Investors residing outside Africa entirely, including in supported countries across Europe, Asia, the Middle East, and the Americas, can sign up but cannot currently complete identity verification through this route. Once eligibility is confirmed, the process involves selecting citizenship, providing an African address, verifying identity with a passport and photo, setting a PIN, providing next-of-kin details, and completing a short investment profile, then funding a USD wallet (minimum $100) via Misan or a card, and subscribing to the Dangote Refinery IPO at ₦525 per share with a minimum of 10 shares, with zero commission on the investment itself. Bamboo is registered with Nigeria's SEC as a Digital Sub-Broker, with South Africa's FSCA as a Category 1 Financial Services Provider, and with FINRA in the US through its affiliate Bamboo Securities LLC; it also operates through partnerships with Tenth Capital in Ghana and Kestrel Capital in Kenya.
